title: 1971, Noakhali
author: Chaitali Sengupta
text:
Noakhali is a landmine in her memory
that only reels backward. Sits like a

land spreading its river of sorrow. A land
thrice partitioned. Each time she shuts

her eyes, a trail like breadcrumbs of fear lead
her back. What happened to Zoya, my

daughter? Who knows who took her away?
Who knows where she sleeps? And her

brother? What have you done to them? Who`ll
bring my message to them? In the naked

sunlight of a Kolkata camp, she sits, sticking to
the lamppost, like a flapping poster. Draping

a hand over her breasts. Raped, like her land.

Nameless, counting the scars of hell. The stories
she saved from 1971, knotted at the end of her

sari squeezed into the tiniest of knots. Lest she
may forget. Stories of people gone missing.

Like the lace torn off the hem of her grey petticoat.
Gone. Disappeared in a gaping hole.

Killed like mosquitoes. Countless times, she murmurs
the names of every single lost soul.

A database of death. Lives torn to bits, reduced to figures.
Like the abandoned pages of history,

long archived. Refusing acknowledgement. Her abused
flesh knows no hope of escape. It sits like

a stringless, torn kite, forever exiled on the tramlines.
